This DHI package backports the upstream fix from systemd v258.9 (commit a8feb2f23565d39df5c90a753c851c1934a53117) before building. The patch rejects non-normalized cgroup paths in the systemd-oomd ManagedOOM varlink handler, closing the path traversal that allowed local users to terminate arbitrary processes.

DHI alsa-lib 1.2.14-1+dhi3 backports upstream commit 536dd6f8affdf5197c12a63a71c92a70b2833cc0. The patch checks get_nonwhite() failures in parse_def() and transfers cleanup to the existing error path, preventing the duplicate snd_config_delete() that causes CVE-2026-56109.

CVE-2026-56392 is an integer overflow in unexpand buffer allocation that multiplies max_column_width by MB_LEN_MAX. That allocation path was introduced after coreutils 9.7 (multibyte expand/unexpand support; first present in 9.11). Debian trixie and this DHI package ship 9.7, which still allocates with ximalloc(max_column_width) and does not contain the vulnerable multiply.
The DHI coreutils package backports the upstream uniq -w multibyte find_field() fix from commit d64e35a8a4c0e4608321433e0d84d917e4e36371.

CVE-2026-54696 affects the json gem's C extension parser. Logstash uses JRuby, which implements JSON parsing in Java without using the vulnerable C extension code. The json gem in JRuby serves only as a compatibility shim and does not contain the vulnerable parser implementation.

GHSA-mhm7-754m-9p8w affects jackson-databind 2.21.4 and is fixed in 2.21.5, which is not yet published to Maven Central. The vulnerability involves authorization issues in polymorphic deserialization. Logstash will be updated to 2.21.5 when it becomes available.

CVE-2026-59889 affects jackson-databind 2.21.4 and 3.1.4, and is fixed in 2.21.5 and 3.1.5 respectively, which are not yet published to Maven Central. The vulnerability involves incorrect authorization in polymorphic deserialization. Logstash will be updated when the fixed versions become available.

CVE-2026-54515 affects jackson-databind 2.18.8 and 2.21.4, and is fixed in 2.18.9 and 2.21.5 respectively, which are not yet published to Maven Central. The vulnerability involves polymorphic deserialization. Logstash will be updated when the fixed versions become available.
